Value.basis: Nothing in the video shows an unlock screen, so this is an inference from what the run itself displays: Ascension 10 on Ironclad, the Underdocks act variant, and a seeded standard run. The act variant is the part that is measured rather than argued - this build's ACT.UNDERDOCKS reports itself locked under UnlockState.none and unlocked under UnlockState.all - so the run on screen could not have been played without it. A creator that far in is assumed to have the rest. The assumption is load-bearing and is recorded as a caveat on every verification this manifest produces.

Evidence.note: Unlock state is never rendered on screen. Measured effect of getting it wrong: replaying this run against UnlockState.none instead of UnlockState.all moves the upfront RNG counter from 412 to 370, changes the act's generated encounters, and locks ACT.UNDERDOCKS outright.

Act 1's identity is read from the map screen, which titles it 'Underdocks'. This build ships two acts at index 0 - Overgrowth and Underdocks - and Overgrowth is the default, so taking the default would have replayed a different run. Acts 2 and 3 are not read from the video; the build ships exactly one variant at each of those indices, which is why the whole list is marked inferred rather than observed.

mods.name: Slay the Relics Exporter
mods.role: Exports relic and HUD state for a stream overlay to read.
mods.replay_risk: Reads game state and writes it outward. No content, no gameplay hooks. The lowest risk of the three, and the only one whose purpose is incompatible with changing anything.

mods.name: BaseLib
mods.role: The community modding framework most StS2 mods build on.
mods.replay_risk: Infrastructure: hook registration, config UI, menu surfaces. Ships in lockstep with the game. It adds no gameplay content of its own, but it is a patching framework, so 'adds nothing' is a statement about this version rather than about the category.

mods.name: Hindsight
mods.role: Resumes a past run from a chosen floor in run history.
mods.replay_risk: The one that can invalidate a reconstruction outright. A resumed run has the same seed, build, content hash and acts as a fresh one, so no environment gate would notice - the recording would simply not start where the history says it does. Defended against directly by source.run_start rather than by argument.

Evidence.method: The count is observed: the game's version overlay reads MODDED (3) throughout. The three identities were established by a separate investigation of this creator's environment and are not readable from the video, which names no mod anywhere. Recorded as an inference for that reason.
Evidence.note: The content hash is kept as a separate and necessary gate. It checks content ids contributed by mods that declare themselves gameplay-affecting; it is blind to a behaviour patch and to a mod declaring itself non-gameplay. Naming the environment does not make the hash an environment fingerprint, and it does not by itself establish that these three changed nothing.

source.coverage: Run start through the end of the first combat: Neow's blessing, the move to the first map node, and every card the player played and every turn they ended across the four turns of the fight, up to and including the killing blow. It stops there. The fight is the unit the comparison contract is defined over, so the history ends where the fight does and nothing after the victory - the loot, the card reward, the next map move - is transcribed.
